claims.text: Increasing Al content in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys promotes local lattice distortion.
Increasing Al content promotes short-range chemical ordering and nanoscale ordered precipitates.
Local lattice distortion and chemical ordering stabilize the phase structure.
Phase stabilization governs the balance between a disordered solid solution and ordered or dual-phase microstructures.
The resulting phase balance supports high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
The baseline low-to-moderate-Al alloy predominantly exhibits a single-phase solid solution.
The baseline alloy lacks significant nanoscale precipitation.
Elevated Al content increases atomic-size mismatch.
Al-induced atomic-size mismatch produces local lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortion favors short-range chemical ordering and nanoprecipitate formation.
The proposed microstructural modification delays deleterious phase separation and coarsening.
Delayed phase separation and coarsening help maintain high-temperature mechanical performance, oxidation resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
Within the targeted moderate range, increasing Al will measurably increase the fraction of nanoscale ordered precipitates relative to the baseline.
Within the targeted moderate range, increasing Al will improve high-temperature strength relative to the baseline.
Within the targeted moderate range, increasing Al will improve radiation tolerance relative to the baseline.
The increased-Al alloys will retain acceptable environmental resistance and cryogenic toughness.
Exceeding a critical Al threshold may cause excessive ordering or coarse intermetallic-phase formation.
Excessive ordering or coarse intermetallic phases may degrade the desired properties.
